s: Which one of the following is not a protein ?
x: Keratin is a fibrous protein forming the main structural constituent of hair, nails etc. Fibroin is an insoluble protein present in silk-produced by the larvae of Bombyx mori. Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular space in the various connective tissues in the body. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide.

s: Which of the following are water-soluble vitamins ?
x: B-group vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble, while A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so B and C is the right pair; D and A are fat-soluble.

s: Golden Rice is a rich source of :
x: Golden Rice is engineered to contain beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A.

x: Diseases related with deficient intake of vitamins are as follows : • Vitamin B1 (Thiamin) – Beri-beri, Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome • Vitamin D (Ergocalciferol, Cholecalciferol) – Rickets and Osteomalacia • Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) – Scurvy

s: Which of the following vitamin helps in blood clotting in humans?
Which of the following vitamins is essential for normal vision?
x: Vitamin A is the name of a group of fat-soluble retinoids, including retinol, retinal, and retinyl esters. Vitamin A is involved in immune function, vision, reproduction, and cellular communication. Vitamin A is critical for vision as an essential component of rhodopsin, a protein that absorbs light in the retinal receptors, and because it supports the normal differentiation and functioning of the conjunctival membranes and cornea. Vitamin A deficiency may lead to 'night blindness'. Vitamin A also supports cell growth and differentiation, playing a critical role in the normal formation and maintenance of the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs.

s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
x: Deficiency of retinol i.e. vitamin A, leads to Xerophthalmia. Lack of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) causes pernicious anaemia and lack of vitamin D (Cholecalciferol 'D3' and Ergocalciferol 'D2') causes rickets in children. Beri-beri is caused by lack of vitamin 'B1' i.e. thiamin not due to lack of tocopherol (vitamin 'E').

s:
Consider the following pairs : Vitamin Deficiency disease
1. Vitamin C : Scurvy
2. Vitamin D : Rickets
3. Vitamin E : Night blindness Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: Scurvy is a disease resulting from the deficiency of vitamin C. Rickets is a nutritional disorder that can develop due to deficiency of vitamin D while vitamin A deficiency can lead to night blindness. So it is clear that only pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched.

s: Which one of the following is the richest source of protein?
x: Among the given options, groundnut is the richest source of protein. Rice is the best source of carbohydrate and apple is known for the richness of antioxidants.

s: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?
x: Among the given options, rice has the highest percentage of carbohydrates.

s: Which one of the following vitamins is helpful in keeping a dream in memory for a longer duration?
x: Taking vitamin B6, vitamin B12 or folate (Vitamin B9) may have an impact on the quality of a person’s dreams and his ability to recall them.

s: Which one of the following compounds is not a vitamin?
x: Niacin – Vitamin B5, Riboflavin –Vitamin B2 and Pyridoxine – Vitamin B6 are vitamins while Thyroxine is a hormone secreted by the thyroid gland (biggest endocrine gland of a human) located in the neck.

s: Hair is composed of protein called –
x: Hair is composed of the protein keratin, which is also the primary component of finger and toe nails.

s: Golden rice is a richer source of –
x: Golden Rice is engineered to produce beta carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A, so vitamin A is the answer.

s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: Milk contains none of the B vitamins
Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency leads to the dry and
One of the symptoms of scurvy is pain in the joints
Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency can lead to heart
x: Milk generally contains vitamins of the B vitamin group such as Thiamin (B1), Riboflavin (B2), Niacin (B3), Cobalamin (B12), Folate (B9) and Pyridoxine (B6). Thus statement of option (a) is incorrect while other given statements are correct.

s: For which desirable character the transgenic crop ‘Golden Rice’ is produced ?
x: Golden Rice is a transgenic crop made to contain beta carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, to fight vitamin A deficiency.

s: Which one of the following is an important source of vitamin E?
x: The Wheat germ oil is extracted from the germ of the wheat kernel which makes up only about 2.5% by weight of the kernel. Wheat germ oil has the highest content of vitamin E. It is a fat-soluble vitamin and plays a role as an antioxidant in the body.

s: Which one of the following food materials contains all essential amino acids?
x: Egg is the best source of all the essential amino acids for human nutrition because it has the highest Biological Value (BV). The Biological Value (BV) is a scale of measurement used to determine what percentage of a given nutrient source is utilized by the body. BV (for protein sources) is derived from providing a measure intake of protein, then determining the nitrogen uptake versus nitrogen excretion. When a protein source contains the essential amino acids in a proportion similar to that required by the body, it has a high BV, while when one or more of the essential amino acids are missing or present in low numbers, it has a low BV. The Biological Value of some protein sources is given in the following table : Protein Source Biological Value Whole egg – 94 Milk – 90 Quinoa – 83 Fish – 76 Beef – 74 Soyabeans – 73

s: Which of the following vitamins is mainly responsible for blood coagulation in human being?
x: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting (its deficiency causes slow clotting), so it is the vitamin responsible for coagulation.

s: Which of the following vitamin is effective in blood clotting?
x: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting and its deficiency causes slow clotting; vitamins A, B and C do not have this role.

s: Which of the following vitamins contain cobalt –
x: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin. It contains a metallic ion cobalt. Its chemical formula is C63H88CoN14O14P. It functions as a cofactor for enzymes in the metabolism of amino acids and fatty acids, required for new cell synthesis, normal blood formation and neurological function. Its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia, nervous system abnormality etc.

s: Kwashiorkor, a form of malnutrition, is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
x: Kwashiorkor is a form of acute malnutrition that occurs due to protein deficiency in the diet. It can cause swelling, loss of appetite, lack of muscle and fat tissues, and an enlarged liver. It usually affects infants and children, most often around the age of weaning through age 5 years. The disease is seen in very severe cases of starvation and poverty-stricken regions worldwide.

s: Deficiency of which vitamin can cause night blindness?
x: Vitamin A is needed by the retina of the eye in the form of retinol, which combines with protein opsin to form rhodopsin, the light absorbing molecules necessary for both low light (scotopic vision) and colour vision.

s: Which of the following has the highest content of Vitamin C ?
x: Guava has the most vitamin C of the four, about 200+ mg per 100 g, against about 50 mg for orange, about 36 mg for mango and about 6 mg for carrot.

s: Which one of the following vitamins is formed in skin in the presence of sunlight?
x: Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin when exposed to sunlight (UV), which is why it is called the sunshine vitamin; vitamins A, K and E are not made this way.

s: The main source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
x: Vitamin A is the major constituent of milk and ghee which are enriched by fats while pulses are the rich source of protein. Raw and citrus fruits are major source of vitamin C.

s: Cyanocobalamin is –
x: Cyanocobalamin is a manufactured form of vitamin B12 which is used to treat vitamin B12 deficiency.

s: Which of the following vitamins are fat soluble?
x: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, while vitamin C and B-group vitamins (such as B12) are water-soluble, so 'A and D' is the correct pair.

s: Silk fibre, hairs, nails and claw are made of –
x: Silk fibre, hairs, nails and claw are made with keratin proteins.

s: Riboflavin deficiency causes which of the following diseases?
x: The riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency (also known as ariboflavinosis) causes skin disorders, hyperemia (excess blood) and edema of the mouth and throat, angular stomatitis (lesions at the corners of the mouth), cheilosis (swollen, cracked lips), hair loss, reproductive problems, sore throat, itchy and red eyes, and degeneration of the liver and nervous system. People with riboflavin deficiency typically have deficiencies of other nutrients, so some of these signs and symptoms might reflect these other deficiencies.

s:
Assertion (A) : Human diet should compulsorily contain glycine, serine and tyrosin.
Reason (R) : Essential amino acids can not be synthesized in the human body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: Glycine, serine and tyrosine are non-essential amino acids, which are synthesized inside our bodies. There are 20 biologically active amino acids found in human body. These are divided into two categories – 10 are essential amino acids and 10 are non-essential amino acids. The amino acids, which can be synthesised in the human body, are known as non-essential amino acids. Essential amino acids are those which can't be synthesized in the human body and must be obtained through diet. Hence, (A) is false, but (R) is true.

s:
Assertion (A) : If somebody stops taking green vegetables hewill suffer from night blindness.
Reason (R) : He will suffer from vitamin A deficiency.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct
x: Green vegetables are a source of vitamin A, whose deficiency causes night blindness, so both A and R are true and R explains A.

s: Which one of the following is not an genetic disease?
x: Night blindness is not a genetic disease. The cause of Night blindness is deficiency of vitamin A. Albinism is genetic disease in which the pigments called melanin is partially or completely absent in the skin, hair and eyes. Haemophilia is a genetic sex-linked disease. Colour blindness is also a genetic disease.

s: The Deficiency of Vitamin D causes the disease :
x: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children, while beri-beri is caused by a vitamin B1 deficiency.

s: The nutritional deficiency condition that needs to be given top priority for remedial action in India today is :
x: Xerophthalmia, caused by severe vitamin A deficiency, is described by, pathological dryness of conjunctiva and cornea. Cells of cornea get dried, keratinized and vision power affected. That’s why remedial action for Xeropthalmia should be prioritized.

s: Which of the following vitamins is known as ergocalciferol?
x: Vitamin D2 is ergocalciferol (D3 is cholecalciferol, the 'chole-' form), so option 1 is correct.

s: Seaweeds are an important source of which one of the following?
x: Seaweed is a type of algae that grows in salt water and (like terrestrial plants) needs sunlight to thrive. There are over ten thousand varieties of seaweed, many of which are good to eat. Seaweeds are best known as the richest natural source of iodine.

s: Alpha-keratin is a protein, present in :
x: Alpha-keratin is a family of fibrous structural proteins. It is the key structural material making up the outer (epidermis) layer of human skin. It is the primary component of hair, nails, hooves, and it provides the necessary strength and toughness for masticatory organs, such as the tongue and the hard palate.

s:
Consider the statements :
Assertion (A) : Vitamin B12 remains stored in liver for about 3-5 years.
Reason (R) : Vitamin B12 is water-soluble.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: Vitamin B12 is also known as cobalamin which is water-soluble and remains stored in the liver for about 3-5 years. Vitamin B12 is a co-factor of DNA synthesis and in both fatty acid and amino acid metabolism. It is particularly important for the normal functioning of the nervous system via its role in the synthesis of myelin and in the maturation of developing RBC in the bone marrow. It contains cobalt (Co).

s: If a person only takes milk, egg and bread in diet, so he may suffer from the disease :
x: If a person only takes milk, egg and bread in his diet then definitely he will suffer from a deficiency of vitamin C which causes scurvy disease. Scurvy causes spongy and bleeding gums loose and falling teeth, the fragility of blood vessels and skin haemorrhages.

s: Which of the following vitamins does not get stored in the body?
x: The body cannot store vitamin C. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, which means they bond with fat molecules and can be stored in the body’s organs (particularly the liver), tissues or blood for long periods of time. Vitamin C, on the other hand is actually water-soluble and bonds instead of water, which is flushed out of the body via the urine rather quickly.

s: Which of the following facts is NOT correct about vitamins?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesized by intestinal
Some vitamins are stored in body
x: Vitamin A, D, E and K are fat-soluble vitamins while B group vitamins and vitamin C are soluble in water. Thus, option (d) is not correct. Facts given in other options are correct about vitamins.

s: The richest source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
x: Orange (citrus fruit) is a well-known rich source of vitamin C. The notes name amla as the richest source, but it is not among the options, so orange is the correct choice.

s: Golden rice is rich in –
x: Golden Rice is genetically engineered to contain beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, so the answer is vitamin A.

s: Which one of the following groups of diet provides maximum energy to human body?
x: Among the given groups of diet, group of Carbohydrate, Fat and Protein provides maximum energy to human body.

s: The disease caused by deficiency of protein in children is–
x: Our liver stores glycogen to fulfil body’s requirement of glucose for energy in between meals. This storage is recouped after every meal. If the meal is delayed further, the body starts consuming its fat reserve and proteins. This condition is starvation. Prolonged starvation causes Marasmus due to a generalized wasting of the body because of both energy and protein deficiency. Due to this, the body of children becomes lean and weak, eyes depressed and skin wrinkled.

s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes following disease :
x: Polishing rice removes the bran that holds the B vitamins, causing thiamine (B1) deficiency, which leads to beri-beri. Rickets, anaemia and goitre are due to other deficiencies.

s: The vitamin available from sun rays is –
x: Skin synthesises vitamin D when exposed to the UV rays in sunlight, so vitamin D is the 'sunshine vitamin'.

s: Which of the following vitamins is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons?
x: Vitamin 'K' is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons. This vitamin is called antihemorrhagic factor. Operation of persons with deficiency of vitamin K can not be done easily because there is a fear of excess bleeding.

s: The substance responsible for bread-making quality in wheat is –
x: Gluten is the protein composite, found in wheat. Gluten gives elasticity to dough, helping its growth and keep its shape and often gives the final product a chewy texture.

s: Which one of the following proteins is present in human hair and nails?
x: Keratin is an extremely strong protein that is a major component in skin, hair, nails, hooves, horns and teeth.

s: Milk is a poor source of :
x: Milk is considered a complete food because it provides protein, vitamin A, vitamin B1, B2, B3, B6, B12, B9, carbohydrate, calcium and potassium etc. Milk contains very small amounts of vitamin C. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

s: Which of the following is synthesized by intestinal bacteria?
x: & (c) Vitamin B12 and vitamin K both are synthesized by bacteria in human intestine.

s: Casein is milk :
x: Casein is a phosphoprotein, which is found in milk. Phosphoprotein means any protein containing bound phosphate. The white colour of the milk is also due to the presence of casein. Some of the other proteins like lactoglobulin and lactalbumin are also found in milk.

s: Which vitamin is soluble in water?
The vitamin which is found in citrus fruits and is necessary for maintaining healthy skin is –
x: Vitamin C occurs in good quantity in various citrus fruits like lemon, orange, Indian gooseberry (amla) etc. Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin which is necessary for normal growth and development and for maintaining healthy skin. Ascorbic acid is the chemical name of Vitamin C. Deficiency of this vitamin causes the disease scurvy in human.

s: Which compound present in D.N.A. does not form amino acid ?
x: Tyrosine or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 22 amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins. Its codons are UAC and UAU. It is a non-essential amino acid with a polar side group. It was first discovered in 1846 by German chemist Justus von Liebig in the protein casein from cheese. It is called tyrosyl when referred to as a functional group or side chain.

Polycarbonate is used for making CDs
Acrylic is also called artificial silk as it is prepared
Teflon is used for coating non-stick kitchenwares
x: Rayon is soft, lustrous and absorbent which exactly copies the characteristics of silk. Rayon appears and feels like silk. Hence, Rayon is called artificial silk. Fibre obtained by chemically treating wood pulp is called rayon or artificial silk. Acrylic fibers are the synthetic fibers which resemble natural wool. Statements of other options are correct.

s: Which one of the following is not formed in our body?
x: Vitamin A cannot be synthesized by the human body.

s: The common name of the chemical compound 'Cholecalciferol' is :
x: Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3 (D3 is 'chole-', D2 'ergo-calciferol'), so the answer is Vitamin D.

s: Recently scientists discovered protein which is responsible for hazardous neural disease Alzheimer’s. Which of the following is that protein?
x: The protein which is responsible for the severe neural Alzheimer’s disease is β-amyloid precursor protein.

s: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :
x: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting; its deficiency causes slow clotting. Vitamins A, B and D do not have this role.

s: Which of the following is the richest source of vitamin A?
x: Mango is a rich source of vitamin A among all the given fruits. It is also rich in vitamin C and E.

s: Most of the enzymes are :
x: Most enzymes are biological catalysts made of proteins, so (1) is correct; they are not lipids, acids or alkalis.

s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes the following disease
x: White rice is milled rice that had its husk, bran, and germ removed. After milling, the rice is polished, resulting in a seed with a bright, white, shiny appearance. The milling and polishing processes of polished rice both remove nutrients. A diet based on polished rice leaves many people vulnerable to the neurological disease beriberi, due to a deficiency of thiamine (Vitamin B1). Adopted over brown rice in the second half of the 19th century because it was favoured by traders, white rice has led to a beriberi epidemic in Asia (Including British India).

s: Some vitamins are fat soluble while others are water soluble. Which of the following are water soluble :
o: Vitamin A, D, E and K
x: B-group vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble, whereas A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only 'Vitamin B and C' is correct.

s: The major food fuel during exercise of long duration is
x: The major food fuel during exercise of high intensity and long duration is carbohydrate.

s: Among the following vegetables, the maximum Vitamin C is found in :
x: Among the above vegetables, the maximum vitamin C is found in chilli. Vitamin C present in each 100 gram of chilli, pumpkin, pea and radish is about 143.7, 9, 40 and 14.8 milligram respectively.

s: Which of the following vitamin's deficiency causes disease of slow blood coagulation ?
x: Vitamin K is a responsible factor for blood clotting or coagulation. Without vitamin K, blood coagulation is seriously impaired and uncontrolled bleeding occurs. Vitamin K is known as antihemorrahgic factor.

s: Which one of the following contains more vitamin A content ?
x: Carrot is the richest source of vitamin A. Spinach is a major source of iron which contributes to the level of haemoglobin concentration, beneficial for oxygen transportation.

s: In countries where polished rice is the mean cereal in their diet, people suffer from –
x: Polished rice loses the B vitamins (thiamine, B1) from the bran, so people relying on it get beri-beri. Pellagra is due to B3, scurvy to C and osteomalacia to D deficiency.

s: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
x: Amla is the richest source of vitamin C, richer than orange, apple or carrot.

s: Which of the following proteins is found in milk ?
x: Casein is the main protein of milk. Agglutinin, myosin and haemoglobin are not milk proteins.

s: Which one of the following compounds is not stored in human body –
x: Unlike some macronutrients, including fats and starches, amino acids are not stored in human body and must be replenished daily through dietary intake. Proteins are polymers of amino acids.

s: The chemical name of Vitamin C is –
x: Vitamin C is chemically ascorbic acid, and its deficiency causes scurvy; thiamine is vitamin B1.

x: Plant sterols (stigmasterol, sitosterol etc.) resembling cholesterol are called phytosterols, whereas animal fats contain cholesterol.

II. Phosphorus

III. Zinc
Which of the above elements are required for maintaining the healthy human body?
x: Cobalt is part of vitamin B12 (cobalamin); phosphorus and zinc are also essential minerals, so all three are required.

s: Which one of the following is useful in the treatment of scurvy disease?
x: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C deficiency, and amla (Aonia, the Indian gooseberry) is the richest source of vitamin C; mango is a vitamin A source.

s: Glucose is a source of energy, which one of the following types of molecule is glucose ?
x: Glucose is a simple sugar, i.e. a carbohydrate, which is the main energy source of the body.

Some vitamins are stored in body.
vitamin K is a water soluble vitamin.

Fruits and vegetables make a good choice because their energy content is high.
A balanced diet must contain plenty of fat and protein with little carbohydrates and fibre.
An optimal quantity of fat, protein carbohydrate with adequate amount of water and fibre makes a healthy diet.

s: Which of the following is known as energy currency for cellular process?
Which one of the following is not a genetic disorder?
x: Xerophthalmia results from vitamin A deficiency, a nutritional cause, not an inherited genetic disorder like colour blindness, Down's syndrome or haemophilia.

s: Which of the following disease is caused by severe deficiency of proteins?

x: Vitamin B12 is cobalamin, containing cobalt, so the complexing metal ion is Co3+.

s: Which of the following is a fat soluble vitamin that plays a role in blood clotting, bone metabolism and regulating blood calcium levels?
Which of the following are required for the formation of bones and teeth?
Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin ……
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency causes megaloblastic/pernicious anaemia; B1 causes beri-beri and B2 causes cheilosis.

s: Deficiency of ………… causes rickets disease.
x: Vitamin D (calciferol) deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

s: What taste do starchy substances have?
x: Starch is a carbohydrate that breaks down to sugars, so starchy foods taste sweet; the notes do not state this directly.

s: How do carbohydrates taste?
x: Simple carbohydrates such as glucose, fructose and sucrose have a characteristically sweet taste.

s: Lutein is a/an:
x: Lutein is a yellow-coloured carotenoid pigment of the xanthophyll class found in plants, egg yolks and vegetables.

s: Which mineral element is present in Vitamin B-12?
x: Vitamin B12 is cobalamin, which contains the mineral cobalt.

s: Which of the following accounts for the red colour of tomato?
x: The red colour of tomato (Lycopersicon esculentum) fruit is due to the carotenoid pigment lycopene. The red colour formation in the apple skin is due to the formation of anthocyanin pigments. The red-orange colour of carrot is due to the pigment β-Carotene.

s: Which one of the following is a rich source of iron?
x: Spinach, a green leafy vegetable, is a rich source of iron; carrot, pea and rice contain much less.

s: Among the following which fruit is a rich source of iron?
x: The fruit karonda is a rich source of iron, so it is sometimes used in the treatment of anaemia.It contains a fair amount of vitamin C which helps in healing wounded therefore is an antiscorbutic.

s: Which of the following gives maximum energy in metabolic processes?
x: Fats have the highest energy value since 1g of fat contains 9.3 kcal of energy; one gram of proteins contains about 4.0 kcal and one gram of carbohydrates also contains about 4.0 kcal of energy.

s: In which category of food is the most amount of calories per unit –
x: Fats have highest calorie value per unit. 4.0 Kcal energy is obtained by metabolic oxidation of 1 gm carbohydrate or protein whereas about 9.3 Kcal is received from fats of the same amount. Flora and fauna, both are a source of fats.

s: Which one of the following is not a natural source of Vitamin A ?
x: Mango, papaya, and carrot are the natural sources of vitamin A, while milk is not a natural source of vitamin A. Milk contains very small amount of vitamin A.

s: The best source of Vitamin C is :
x: Indian gooseberry (amla) is the richest source of vitamin C (Ascorbic acid). Orange, tomato, lemon, papaya, peas, etc. are also good sources of vitamin C. It is an important antioxidant which helps to protect against cancer, heart disease, stress, maintaining a healthy immune system and wound healing process. It is essential for sperm production and formation of collagen. The collagen protein involved in the building and health of cartilage, joints, skin and blood vessels etc.

s: Protein requirement of young and old person are –
o: Higher in the young and lower in the old
Higher in the old and lower in the young
Very high in the young and very low in the old
x: Elderly individuals are more likely to be influenced by various biological, environmental and social factors. This would result to increase protein needs for adults as compared to younger one. Thus in practice, the protein needs of elderly people are probably higher than that for the young.

s: Vitamin 'C' help in absorption of which of following elements?
x: Vitamin C is helpful in iron absorption whereas vitamin D helps in absorption of magnesium and calcium.

s: Besides proteins and carbohydrates, other elements of nutritional value found in milk, include :
x: Milk contains about 87% water. It has proteins, vitamin A, vitamin B12, B1, B3, B9, B6 and Riboflavin, carbohydrates, calcium (Ca) and potassium (K) etc. Thus, milk is an ideal diet containing almost all nutritious elements. Milk contains only a trace amount of iron.

s: Which one among these is related to the deficiency of potassium ?
x: Lack of potassium in the body causes low blood pressure. It is a mineral whose major sources are flesh, milk, cereals, fruits and vegetables.

s: Choose wrong statement regarding proteins :
o: We obtain proteins from both animals and plants
Proteins are made of amino acids
About 30 percent of our body weight comes from
Proteins are called building blocks of our body
x: Proteins are called building blocks of our body. As per the NCERT, about 20 percent of our body weight comes from proteins. Proteins are essential for growth and repair of muscle and other body tissues. Proteins are made of amino acids that contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. We obtain proteins from animal as well as vegetable sources. Proteins of animal origin are found in milk, eggs, cheese, fish and meat. Proteins from these sources contain all the essential amino acids (EAA) in adequate amounts. Vegetable proteins are found in pulses (legumes), cereals, beans, nuts, oilseeds, etc.

s: The source of vitamin D is –
x: The source of vitamin D is sun rays. In fact, vitamin D is synthesized in our dermal cells by sun rays which is released in the blood. Besides of sun rays, vitamin D is also obtained from butter, the yolk of egg, liver, and kidney, etc. Rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults occur due to deficiency of vitamin D. Together with calcium, deficiency of vitamin D causes osteoporosis in older adults.

Reason (R) : Vitamins are essential for proper growth of the body.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
x: Most of the vitamins cannot be synthesized in the human body, so they are considered as essential food factors.
